simple.meaning: מִפְקָד (miphqâd) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “an appointment , i.e. mandate ; concretely, a designated spot ; specifically, a census.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Ezekiel, beginning at 2 Samuel 24:9. Its contexts include family, offering, kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מִפְקָד (H4662).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

structuredEvidence.definition: an appointment , i.e. mandate ; concretely, a designated spot ; specifically, a census

firstOccurrence.englishText: Joab gave up the sum of the counting of the people to the king: and there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men who drew the sword; and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.

majorEvents.label: Offering
majorEvents.evidenceText: You shall also take the bull of the sin offering, and it shall be burned in the appointed place of the house, outside of the sanctuary.

timeline.evidenceText: Joab gave up the sum of the counting of the people to the king: and there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men who drew the sword; and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.

Joab gave up the sum of the census of the people to David. All those of Israel were one million one hundred thousand men who drew a sword; and in Judah were four hundred seventy thousand men who drew a sword.

Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were overseers under the hand of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the ruler of God’s house.
You shall also take the bull of the sin offering, and it shall be burned in the appointed place of the house, outside of the sanctuary.
